title: Reel strips and paylines
summary: Circular arrays, the modulo operator, and reading a line.

cards.title: A reel is a loop
cards.body:
A physical reel is a strip glued into a circle: after the last symbol comes the first. In code that's a **circular array**, and the % operator does the wrap-around:

`strip[(stop + row) % length]`

With 20 stops, stop 19 and row 1 gives (19 + 1) % 20 = 0: back to the start.
Try stops near the end of the strip in the Algorithm Lab, like 19, 18, 19, to see the wrap.

cards.title: Reading a payline
cards.body: Lucky 3 has one payline across the middle row. Only three in a row pays.
With wilds, the first non-wild symbol decides what the line is "about", and wilds extend the chain. (Real games add rules, e.g. comparing a pure-wild line's own pay, but the core loop is this one.)

cards.question: A strip has 22 stops. The reel stops at 21. Which strip index shows in the bottom row (row 2)?
